sections.h2: Who to call about Bradley County property tax
sections.html:
Your tax passes through two county desks. The Assessor of Property decides what a parcel is worth and takes appeals. The Trustee mails the bills and takes the money, with no say over assessed value.

  • Assessor of Property: Courthouse Annex, 155 Broad Street NW, Room 105, Cleveland. Phone 423-728-7125.
  • Trustee: 1701 Keith Street NW, Cleveland, TN 37311. Phone 423-728-7247. The office keeps hours of 8:30 to 4:30 from Monday through Thursday, and 8:30 to 5 on Friday. Card payments by phone: 833-591-7276.
  • City of Cleveland taxes: the City Clerk, 190 Church Street NE. Phone 423-472-4551.
  • Delinquent tax sales: the Chancery Court Clerk and Master, 423-728-7209.

If your house is inside Cleveland, expect two bills, county and city. A property in Bradley County that lies outside every city receives just the county bill.

Tennessee's formula starts with appraised value, converts it with an assessment ratio, and charges the rate on every $100 of that result. Residential and farm land use 25 percent. Commercial and industrial use 40 percent.

The 2026 net county property tax rate is $1.0772 per $100 of assessed value. County-only properties in the fire service district pay an extra $0.2558, for a combined $1.3330. Charleston adds a city rate of $0.3655, which brings the county and city total to $1.4427. For Cleveland's rate, call the city at 423-472-4551.

What you actually pay depends on the appraisal of your own parcel. Take the appraisal printed on your notice, apply the ratio, then the rate for your address. The assessor's office will explain anything on the notice that looks unclear.

October is when statements go to the January 1 owner, and the last day of February is the deadline. For 2026 taxes that falls on February 27, 2027.

After the deadline the Trustee applies 1.5 percent interest, or 18 percent a year, on the first day of each month beginning March 1. For checks sent through the mail the postmark date controls, and the night deposit box is treated as that same day. Current taxes can be paid in parts by mail or at the counter. A web payment has to be the full amount.

sections.h2: How do you appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the Local Board of Equalization; the assessor's office handles scheduling. A changed appraisal triggers a mailed notice beginning May 20, 2027. The board sits starting June 1, 2027, and the last day to book a time for that session is June 17, 2027.

You or an agent holding your written authorization must be present. If you do not appear and appeal, the assessment becomes final with no further appeal right (T.C.A. 67-5-508). Forms for a letter of authorization and for an informal review are on the assessor's website. The office answers at 423-728-7125 and assessor@bradleycountytn.gov.

A disappointing county ruling can go on to the State Board of Equalization. The filing window closes August 1 of the tax year, or 45 days after the county board's notice was sent, whichever comes last.

For low-income elderly owners, disabled owners and disabled veteran owners, Tennessee refunds part or all of the local tax on a primary residence. Because it is a payment made to you and not a cut in the bill, you pay the bill first.

  • Age: 65 or older by December 31 of the tax year.
  • Income: no more than $38,470 combined, based on 2025 income of all living owners of record and the applicant's spouse.
  • Disabled veteran: the first $175,000 of the home's market value is covered.
  • Ownership: show you owned the home during the tax year, with a tax bill, warranty deed or probated will.
  • Timing: new applicants for relief and the tax freeze apply between October 1, 2026 and April 5, 2027.

One primary residence qualifies in a given year. Applications are handed out by the Trustee's office, and 423-728-7247 reaches the relief coordinator.

sections.h2: Before you list a Bradley County house
sections.html:
A little preparation prevents closing-day surprises. Start by learning whether the address sits in Cleveland, in Charleston or in neither, which settles how many bills you owe and whom to phone. Then read your current notice for the appraisal, rate and due date. Next, if you get state relief or the tax freeze, ask the Trustee what a sale does to it.

After that, check whether you are behind. Interest grows monthly once March arrives, and a delinquent parcel can land with the Clerk and Master. Finally, let the title company know early which bills are settled, so the settlement statement comes out correct. Buyers and lenders like proof that taxes are current, and a receipt from the Trustee provides it.

The debt belongs to the parcel. If ownership changes in March, the bill still carries the name of the January 1 owner, and the buyer may ask for a copy. Whatever remains unpaid continues to grow against the property.

The closing statement should show how the year's tax was divided; ask the title company if it does not. Settle any unpaid prior-year tax by closing, because 1.5 percent interest builds monthly after March 1.

Taxes ignored for long enough lead to an auction by the Clerk and Master. The winning bidder waits a year after the sale is confirmed to take possession, redemption interest runs 10 percent a year, and every lien except state and federal ones is wiped out. City delinquent taxes in Cleveland go to the Clerk and Master after 12 months of penalty.

Bradley County had an estimated 115,465 residents in July 2025, with 67.3 percent of homes owner-occupied. If a lender escrows your taxes, pass the county's bill along, since the county does not send it to the lender. Owners who pay directly should keep the receipt for the closing agent.

Back taxes in the way? We buy Bradley County houses as-is and pay the balance from the proceeds at closing, so you do not have to find the money first. The payoff figure comes from the Trustee at 423-728-7247, and it helps to request it early.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 tax rate in Bradley County?
faqs.a: County net rate: $1.0772 per $100 of assessed value, rising to $1.3330 inside the fire service district. In Charleston the county and city combined are $1.4427. Cleveland has its own rate, so call 423-472-4551.

faqs.q: Where can I pay my Bradley County property tax?
faqs.a: Use the Trustee at 1701 Keith Street NW in Cleveland, the phone line 833-591-7276, or the website. Cleveland city tax is paid to the City Clerk, 190 Church Street NE.

faqs.q: When must 2026 Bradley County taxes be paid?
faqs.a: February 27, 2027. From March 1 on, 1.5 percent interest is charged on the first day of each month.

Yes, by mail or at the counter, provided the current year is paid in full by the February due date. Online payments must be the full amount. The partial payment signup window is October 1, 2026 through February 5, 2027.

faqs.q: Who handles questions about my property value?
faqs.a: Phone the Assessor of Property, 423-728-7125. The assessor's office books appeals before the Local Board of Equalization. The Trustee has no power to change an assessment.
